without adequate payment and/or hearing as being illegal

together with interest at the statutory or judicially recognised rate, from the date of deprivation of possession/demolition until the date of actual payment, and pass..."
2. Heard Sri C.B.Adarsh Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner appeared through virtually,
learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue and learned counsel representing for respondent Nos.6 and 7.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that already she made applications for enhancement of the compensation under Section 3(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred as 'the Act') on 19.06.2023 and 09.10.2023.
4.

In view of the same, the respondents concerned are directed to consider the representation/application filed under Section 3(5) of the Act and pass appropriate orders within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
DR,J 5.
Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
